title: [finding] Two spellings for "a hole i18next must NOT fill": `auth.forgotPassword.successDescription` uses `{{email}}`, its sibling three lines away uses `{seconds}`
body:
Measured while building objectui#3845's `interpolation-parity` gate — **not in that PR's scope**, and observation-class: the current behaviour is correct in all ten languages and nothing a user hits today is broken.

## The pattern

Some translated strings are **labels handed to a component as a prop**, and the component substitutes into them itself, after `t()` has already returned. The call site cannot do the substitution because it renders before the value exists. `ForgotPasswordForm` is the case: it takes `labels.successDescription` and fills in the address only once the user has submitted the form.

`packages/auth/src/ForgotPasswordForm.tsx:286`

```js
const successMsg = l.successDescription.includes('{{email}}')
  ? l.successDescription.replace('{{email}}', email)
  : `${l.successDescription} ${email}`;
```

That works because i18next leaves an **unmatched** `{{name}}` in its output verbatim, so the string travels through `t()` with its hole intact and arrives at the component still fillable. All ten packs carry the hole (`en`: `We've sent a password reset link to {{email}}. Please check your inbox.`), so this is the shape in every language, not an `en` quirk.

## The finding: the repo already has a *different* spelling for exactly this

Three lines away in the same labels object, `apps/console/src/pages/auth/ForgotPasswordPage.tsx`, the same pattern is spelled with **single** braces, with a comment saying why:

```
// `{seconds}` (single braces) is the component's own hole — kept out
// of i18next's `{{…}}` interpolation on purpose.
resendOtpCountdownText: t('auth.forgotPassword.resendOtpCountdownText', {
  defaultValue: 'Resend in {seconds}s',
```

So the same concept — *a hole whose filler is downstream of i18next* — has two spellings inside one form's label list, and only one of them is documented as deliberate. The `{{email}}` spelling is indistinguishable, at a glance and to every static tool, from an ordinary i18next hole that somebody simply forgot to pass an argument for.

## Why it matters, and why it is dormant rather than broken

It cost the objectui#3845 census two false positives (both `auth.forgotPassword.successDescription` call sites), which is now handled by an explicit `EXTERNALLY_INTERPOLATED_HOLES` registry in `scripts/check-i18n-call-site-keys.mjs` — an entry with a reason, whose premise is re-verified against both the pack and `ForgotPasswordForm.tsx` by the self-test. That closes the tooling half.

What stays open is the authoring half, and it is a live trap in one specific direction: **passing `email` at the call site would break it.** i18next would consume the hole, `includes('{{email}}')` would then be false, and the fallback branch would append the address a **second** time — `...link to a@b.com. Please check your inbox. a@b.com`. That is precisely the "fix" a reader who does not know about the second stage would reach for on seeing a `{{email}}` with no argument. The gate now reports that argument, so the trap is guarded; the ambiguity that invites it is not removed.

## Options

- **A. Converge on single braces.** Move `{{email}}` to `{email}` in all ten packs and update `ForgotPasswordForm`'s marker. Makes the two spellings one, and makes "this is not i18next's hole" true by construction rather than by convention. Cost: a ten-pack value change, so it moves through `scripts/check-i18n-en-drift.mjs`, and it is a value edit on a string users read.
- **B. Leave the spelling, document it in the pack.** Cheapest; keeps the ambiguity, and a pack comment is not visible from the call site where the mistake gets made.
- **C. Pass the value properly.** Give `ForgotPasswordForm` an `email` prop it interpolates through i18next rather than by string replacement — arguably the contract-first shape, since the two-stage substitution exists only because the label is computed too early. Largest change; touches the auth component's public props.

No recommendation attached — the axes here are a public-prop contract in `@object-ui/auth` and a ten-pack copy edit, both outside what a gate finding should decide.

Related: objectui#3845 (the gate and its registry), objectui#3512 (`createSafeTranslation`'s provider-less interpolation recognises only one of i18next's four hole spellings — same family, different face), objectui#3650 (the en-drift gate option A would move through).
